sources.author: Swyx
sources.headline: AI Researcher & Developer Advocate
sources.post_summary: Discusses the evolution of AI agents from hype to practical deployment, highlighting key frameworks like LangChain and AutoGPT for building autonomous systems. Shares insights on challenges in reliability and scaling agentic workflows. Emphasizes the need for better developer tools to streamline agent orchestration.

sources.author: Andrej Karpathy
sources.headline: Founder at Eureka Labs, ex-OpenAI
sources.post_summary: Explores the infrastructure required for training and deploying large-scale AI models, focusing on GPU clusters and efficient data pipelines. Critiques current AI infra bottlenecks and proposes optimizations for developer workflows. Predicts a shift towards agent-native infrastructure.

sources.author: Nat Friedman
sources.headline: Co-founder at GitHub, Investor in AI
sources.post_summary: Highlights emerging developer tools powered by AI agents for code generation and automation, such as Cursor and Replit AI. Shares examples of how these tools are transforming software development pipelines. Notes the infrastructure demands for real-time agent collaboration.

sources.author: Guillermo Rauch
sources.headline: CEO at Vercel
sources.post_summary: Talks about building AI infrastructure for edge-deployed agents, integrating automation into Next.js workflows. Demonstrates how Vercel's platform reduces latency for AI-driven apps. Advises developers on scaling agent-based automations.

sources.author: Eliot Peper
sources.headline: AI Product Lead at Scale AI
sources.post_summary: Analyzes the rise of multi-agent systems for enterprise automation, detailing tools like CrewAI for orchestration. Discusses infrastructure needs for secure, scalable agent deployments. Provides a roadmap for developers entering the space.

sources.author: Sami Rahman
sources.headline: Founder @ Outbound Factory | Helping founders scale outbound sales with AI automation
sources.post_summary: Discusses building a GTM engineering stack using AI for outbound automation, sharing a framework that reduced CAC by 40% for SaaS companies. Emphasizes integrating sales ops with revops for scalable lead gen. Includes code snippets for custom automation tools.

sources.author: Amy Volas
sources.headline: CEO @ Avenue Talent Partners | Revenue Operations & Sales Leadership Expert
sources.post_summary: Outlines the evolution of revenue operations in 2024, blending sales ops, marketing ops, and customer success for unified GTM strategies. Shares case studies where revops alignment boosted ARR growth by 30%. Advises on tools like HubSpot and Salesforce for integration.

sources.author: Ankur Nagpal
sources.headline: Founder @ Teachable | Carry1st | Building Creator Economies
sources.post_summary: Explains a content strategy playbook for B2B GTM, focusing on LinkedIn and newsletters to drive outbound leads without heavy ad spend. Details how to repurpose sales ops data into viral content threads. Reports 5x engagement lift for his portfolio companies.

sources.author: Kyle Coleman
sources.headline: Head of Sales @ G2 | Ex-Gong | Revenue Ops Advocate
sources.post_summary: Breaks down outbound automation pitfalls in sales ops, recommending a hybrid human-AI approach for GTM motions. Shares metrics from scaling teams at Gong, including reply rates and pipeline velocity improvements. Warns against over-automation leading to spam flags.

sources.author: Sarah Beth Aaronson
sources.headline: VP Revenue Operations @ Lattice | Scaling Startups to $100M ARR
sources.post_summary: Presents a revops framework for content-led GTM, integrating sales ops data to inform strategy. Details how to measure content ROI through pipeline attribution. Includes templates for ops teams to operationalize content flywheels.

sources.author: Pieter Levels
sources.headline: Indie Maker & Founder of Nomad List, Remote OK
sources.post_summary: Pieter shares his journey as a solo developer shipping multiple products like Nomad List and Remote OK without VC funding. He emphasizes the power of building in public, iterating based on user feedback, and achieving profitability through bootstrapping. His post inspires others to start small and ship fast.

sources.author: Arvid Kahl
sources.headline: Serial Entrepreneur, Author of The Embedded Entrepreneur
sources.post_summary: Arvid recounts pivoting from corporate life to solo founding FeedbackPanda, which he built and sold profitably. He details the process of shipping an MVP in weeks, validating with users publicly, and scaling to $80k/month. The post offers practical advice for career pivots into tech entrepreneurship.

sources.author: KP (Karthik Pattabiraman)
sources.headline: Founder of Shipfast, Solo Developer Tools
sources.post_summary: KP describes launching Shipfast, a boilerplate for solo devs to ship Rails apps in days. He built it in public, sharing weekly updates on progress, revenue hitting $20k MRR, and lessons on product-market fit. Encourages builders to document their journey transparently.

sources.author: Sahil Lavingia
sources.headline: Founder & CEO of Gumroad
sources.post_summary: Sahil reflects on his pivot from Pinterest to founding Gumroad as a solo project initially. He discusses shipping the first version publicly, growing to millions in creator payouts, and the importance of community feedback in product development. Post motivates non-traditional tech career paths.

sources.author: Daniel Vassallo
sources.headline: Ex-AWS, Indie Maker, Small Bets Advocate
sources.post_summary: Daniel shares his transition from Amazon engineer to solo building micro-SaaS like Grow with Ward. He highlights shipping 10+ products publicly, most failing but teaching key lessons, with one hitting sustainability. Advocates for small bets over big pivots in tech careers.
